question: Shivam invests a sum of ₹5400 and Rupesh invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Rupesh gets ₹600 more interest than Shivam, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the rate and time are constant, the difference in Simple Interest is directly proportional to the difference in Principal.

Extra Interest = (Extra Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

600 = [(9400 − 5400) × R × 4] ÷ 100

600 = (4000 × R × 4) ÷ 100

160 × R = 600 ⇒ R = 3.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 3.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Shivam's Investment (P₁) = ₹5400

Rupesh's Investment (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 4 years

Difference in interest received = ₹600
